clue.text: Valuable card in identical trick

indicators.note: in tells us the card goes inside the word for identical

parts.note: identical things are the same
the king is a high-ranking, valuable playing card

explanation.surface: A card player pulls off a trick using a pair of matching high cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Valuable card' sounds like a trump or ace, but a king works here. A skin game is chiefly American slang for a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin game is a swindle, a dishonest scheme used to fleece a victim.

clue.text: Set in a strangely messy time

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of messy, plus the time letter, are to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Something is placed, oddly, in an untidy period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges MESSY together with T (time) into the answer; T sits inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a group of things working together as a whole, which is an organised scheme or arrangement.

clue.text: Semblances of time in one piece of writing

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the period of time within the other pieces

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A writer captures the look of an era in a single article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of writing' gives the standard abbreviation for manuscript, and the period of time is split by it rather than added at an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A semblance is an outward likeness or appearance, much as a picture or representation is.

clue.text: Attempt at an instrument of torture by ingenious devices

parts.note: gadge is an obsolete word, found in Chambers and used by Browning, for an instrument of torture
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone tries out a torture instrument made with clever mechanical contraptions.
explanation.walkthrough: GADGE is a rare dictionary word for a torture instrument; the setter expects the solver to know it or build it from the definition. 'at' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collective term for clever mechanical contrivances and gizmos.

clue.text: Pole given pig-food

definitions.meaning: a tall upright spar, as on a ship
beech nuts and acorns fallen in woodland, on which pigs were fed

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's upright spar is a pole, and the fallen nuts of forest trees used as swine fodder share the same name.

clue.text: List of charges for artist back in quarrel

indicators.note: in sets the turned artist within the word for a quarrel

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: back says the artist's letters are read the other way round

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter and someone fall out again over a price list.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist; 'back' turns it before it goes into the quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a schedule of prices or duties payable.

clue.text: Loose as a meaning

parts.note: the drift of a remark is its general meaning

explanation.surface: Something is described as being imprecise in its sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat drifting free of its moorings is loose, unattached and without direction.

clue.text: Insolent as little devil almost removed without study

annotationWithheld.why: Insolent as little devil almost removed without study: IMP and DEN (study) are clear, but no reading of 'almost removed' gives the remaining U...T (or PUT around DEN after IM); likely an OCR misread or a lost word
annotationWithheld.clue: Insolent as little devil almost removed without study

clue.text: Reward pronounced holy for the most faint

parts.note: a fee is a payment or reward for a service

indicators.note: pronounced says the word for holy is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: something holy is blessed

explanation.surface: A payment declared sacred goes to the faintest of claimants.
explanation.walkthrough: BLESSED and BLEST sound the same, so 'pronounced' gives the shorter spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble means faint or weak, so its superlative describes whatever is weakest of all.

clue.text: Friends retreat before the line recklessly

indicators.note: before places the turned friends ahead of the line
to retreat is to go back, so the word for friends is read backwards

parts.note: pals are friends
a dash is a short horizontal line in punctuation

explanation.surface: A group of friends falls back and then charges for the line without caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun but is the verb, telling us to run the friends backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash means carelessly hasty, done without proper thought.

clue.text: Three times left in food

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation for left inside the food

parts.note: tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, eaten as food

explanation.surface: Something was left over in the meal on three occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripe, cow's stomach lining, is a traditional cheap food in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble or threefold describes a quantity multiplied by three.

clue.text: Bad weather, but batting twice in charity

indicators.note: in puts the doubled batting word inside the charity

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity event

indicators.note: twice says the word for batting is written two times

parts.note: in cricket, the side batting is in

explanation.surface: Poor conditions, yet a cricketer bats twice at a charity match.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British student fundraising event, and a cricketer who is batting is said to be in; 'twice' doubles that before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain falling steadily is a spell of wet, unpleasant conditions.

clue.text: It is tiny place, but I am the landlord we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks a phrase taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a landlord can say I let, since letting property is what landlords do

explanation.surface: A small spot belongs to someone who says they own and rent out property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I let' spoken sounds like the answer. 'It is' and 'but' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyelet is a small hole, a little opening for a lace or cord.

clue.text: Play the fool, backing pool

annotationWithheld.why: Play the fool, backing pool: DAFF (play the fool) + ODIL (LIDO reversed) gives the answer, but no word defines the flower; the definition seems lost in the OCR

clue.text: A reason for being stranded

parts.note: grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they are stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for being' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is aground has run onto the shore or seabed and is stuck there.

clue.text: Company without garb for bandit

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the company surrounds the garb

parts.note: a band is a company or group of people
rig is clothing, an outfit or garb

explanation.surface: A troupe with no costume stands in for an outlaw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here has its old sense 'outside', so the company wraps round the garb.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a robber, one of a gang of outlaws in remote country.

clue.text: Hard workers for place without capital

indicators.note: without capital means the first, capital letter is dropped

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Diligent staff are sent to a location that has no money.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS, short for Hampshire, a county in southern England, loses its capital H. 'capital' looks like money but means the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are proverbially industrious insects, the model of diligent labour.

clue.text: If islander loses crop, it will mean rise of shepherd

annotationWithheld.why: If islander loses crop, it will mean rise of shepherd: CORSICAN less CORN leaves SICA, ACIS read upwards; the only wordplay form is CORN around reversed ACIS, and its sole container word 'loses' is a deletion signal the check refuses on a container
annotationWithheld.clue: If islander loses crop, it will mean rise of shepherd

clue.text: Woman has success over a single man

indicators.note: over in a down clue sets the first piece above the next

parts.note: a win is a success
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit
Fred is a man's name

explanation.surface: A woman triumphs over one unmarried man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' suggests unmarried, but gives I, the numeral one. 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Winifred is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Speed and pot strangely hindered

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of speed and pot are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Drugs, amphetamine and cannabis, oddly held someone back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges SPEED and POT; 'and' is no fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to bar or preclude someone, so estopped means prevented.

clue.text: Leave out the thing following an award

indicators.note: following puts the thing after the award

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
it means the thing

explanation.surface: Someone is told to skip whatever comes after an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit is a British honour in the monarch's personal gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out is to exclude or skip, as when something is dropped from a list.

clue.text: Rich son may come from the county

indicators.note: may come signals that the letters of rich son may come out in another order

explanation.surface: A wealthy heir hails from the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may come' rearranges RICH SON. The county is Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall's people and things are described by this adjective, meaning belonging to that county.

clue.text: Elegant tree

definitions.meaning: a conifer of the genus Picea

explanation.definitionFit: A smartly turned-out person is neat and trim, and the same word names an evergreen conifer.

clue.text: For floating voters, tried hard

indicators.note: floating suggests letters drifting loose and rearranging

explanation.surface: Campaigners made a big effort to win over undecided voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'floating' rearranges VOTERS; floating voters are undecided ones. 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, to make a great effort.

clue.text: Tone of voice for a dollar

parts.note: a dollar is a hundred cents, written C (Roman hundred) plus cent

explanation.surface: A singer's tone is bought for a dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: A dollar is 'a C cent', a hundred cents, with C the Roman numeral for 100. 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An accent is the emphasis or inflection given to speech.

clue.text: Cutting amusement

definitions.meaning: missing or omitting, as in cutting a lesson
jumping over a turning rope as a pastime

explanation.definitionFit: Missing class is one sense, and jumping rope for fun, a playground pastime, is another.

clue.text: Literary man with convulsive motion is imaginative

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A writer with a twitch is creative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'is' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic writing is creative and expressive, marked by imagination.

clue.text: Measure for European

definitions.meaning: an old unit of length, five and a half yards

explanation.definitionFit: A rod or perch of five and a half yards is one sense, and a person from Poland is the other.

clue.text: Homer forms half of this collection of literature

annotationWithheld.why: Homer forms half of this collection of literature: Homer gives COR (both Hebrew measures), half the answer, but nothing in the clue gives PUS
annotationWithheld.clue: Homer forms half of this collection of literature

clue.text: Flying manoeuvre left in implement for means of escape

parts.note: a loop is an aerobatic manoeuvre

indicators.note: in puts the left letter inside the implement

parts.note: a hoe is a garden implement

explanation.surface: A pilot's stunt, a tool dropped, a way to get out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside HOE.
explanation.definitionFit: A loophole is an ambiguity in a rule that lets someone evade it.

clue.text: Made a mistake in an odd editorial

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the run of words an odd editorial

explanation.surface: A newspaper's leader column contained a strange error.
explanation.walkthrough: From the saying 'Homer nods', meaning even the greatest make slips.
explanation.definitionFit: To nod is to slip up through a lapse of attention, so made an error.

clue.text: Capital supporter for chief and others

parts.note: a head is a chief or leader
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A city's backer stands up for the leader and everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means head, not a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion on a seat that supports the head, the body's top, is this.
